Finnish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

asua (“to live, reside”) +‎ -nto

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈɑsunto/, [ˈɑ̝s̠un̪t̪o̞]
  • Rhymes: -ɑsunto
  • Syllabification(key): a‧sun‧to
  • Hyphenation(key): asun‧to
This entry needs an audio pronunciation. If you are a native speaker with a microphone, please record this word. The recorded pronunciation will appear here when it's ready.

Noun

[edit]

asunto

  1. home, residence; unit, housing unit, dwelling unit; dwelling, domicile, habitation (any place for living, especially one constructed for that purpose)
    Synonym: asumus
    Near-synonym: koti
  2. (in particular) flat, apartment (complete domicile occupying only part of a building)
    Synonyms: asuinhuoneisto (formal), huoneisto (shorter form of the previous term), (colloquial) kämppä, luukku, boksi
    Hyponym: kerrostaloasunto

Usage notes

[edit]
  • The most common English translation for asunto in a general context is simply "home", although note that "home" in any sentimental sense, or in the sense of the place where someone lives, is koti, not asunto. In official use, the term unit (housing unit, dwelling unit) or dwelling may be used. residence may also be used, but it carries a somewhat formal tone.
    • However, translating 250 asuntoa as "250 dwellings" may imply 250 separate buildings, while the Finnish phrase makes no such implication.
    • Other possible terms include domicile, habitation and abode, but these are chiefly formal or poetic.

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin assūmptus. Cognate with English assumption and English assume.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /aˈsunto/ [aˈsũn̪.t̪o]
  • Audio (Colombia):(file)
  • Rhymes: -unto
  • Syllabification: a‧sun‧to

Noun

[edit]

asunto m (plural asuntos)

  1. matter, issue, business
    Synonyms: materia, cuestión
  2. affair (a romantic relationship)
    Synonym: aventura

Derived terms

[edit]
  • asuntillo
  • asunto pendiente
  • asuntos exteriores
  • tomar cartas en el asunto
